assessment: The bench holds one real card, so nine of the ten are pool scouts, ranked by how directly they plug into the deck's three verified engines: Zada's copy-draw (stack 001), the Empty the Warrens + Impact Tremors storm burst (stack 002), and the Haze of Rage + Storm-Kiln Artist loop (stack 005). Every combo pick here completes a line whose other pieces are already sleeved; none is asserted as working — each needs a stack scenario. Two famous pool hits stayed off on an oracle read: Repercussion pairs with Blasphemous Act but turns the sweeper self-lethal under your own 1/1 swarm, and Glacial Chasm (the pool's lone synergy candidate, a Game Changer) reads 'Creatures you control can't attack' in a deck that wins by attacking wide. The obsolescence channel's leads (Firebolt et al. over Past in Flames) are lower-CMC lookalikes, not replacements for a storm rebuild, and were rejected the same way. Cuts follow strategy:deckbuilding.cutting — 'cut duplicated function before any uncovered class, and cut the ceiling card before the median one.'

combo_lines_opened.produces: Infinite colored mana; Infinitely powerful creatures you control until end of turn; Infinite magecraft triggers; Infinite storm count; Infinite Treasure tokens

ten.why: One red mana, targets only a creature, so Zada copies it per body — and with Storm-Kiln Artist each copy mints a Treasure, which is the same loop shape as the verified Haze of Rage engine (stack 005) at half the entry cost.
ten.unlocks: A second self-sustaining storm loop: buyback {3} recasts against Treasures made per creature, plus +3/+0 to the whole team on every pass. The break-even creature count is exactly what the stack scenario must settle.

ten.why: Mana Geyser, Seething Song, Ruby Medallion and Storm-Kiln Artist are all already in the 99 — one pool card completes three separate infinite-flagged lines through the deck's existing ritual suite.
ten.unlocks: Buyback-copies any ritual mid-storm; even off-combo, copying Mana Geyser or Battle Hymn on the pivot turn (decision 002's fire-the-engine spot) roughly doubles the storm count.

ten.why: Stack 004 examined the combo graph's Krenko + Prospector 'infinite' in this deck and found it assumes Krenko is your commander; Thornbite Staff's death-untap on the equipped creature closes that loop with pieces the deck already runs and no command-zone assumption.
ten.unlocks: Equip Krenko ({4} — he is no Shaman), tap for tokens, Prospector sacrifices one, Krenko untaps: doubling tokens plus red mana, feeding the verified Impact Tremors damage engine (stack 002). Needs its own stack scenario before it is fact.

ten.why: Stack 002 verified Empty the Warrens as the fourth spell dealing 8 to each opponent through Impact Tremors; Purphoros is a second, indestructible copy of that trigger at 2 damage per token — the same storm turn deals 24 per head instead of 8.
ten.unlocks: Redundancy for the deck's verified token-to-damage conversion, on a body sweepers and creature removal cannot touch while devotion stays low.

ten.why: With Zada on the field it is both modes: {R} per card in an opponent's hand plus impulse three — the single biggest storm-turn accelerant in the colour, and this deck's whole plan is one explosive pivot turn.
ten.unlocks: Ritual plus fuel in one card; a turn-4 Empty the Warrens for 10+ tokens becomes routine. It is a Game Changer — the computed floor stays 4, but the pilot should know it deepens the tier-4 read.

ten.why: It targets only one creature, so cast on Zada it is copied to every attacker: team-wide double strike halves the board size the verified Fists of Flame lethal (stack 003) needs to close.
ten.unlocks: A one-card combat kill layer — mid-combat, after blocks, ten 1/1s hit for 20; stacked with a copied Fists of Flame the same swing is usually lethal to the table.

ten.why: Howlsquad Heavy's max-speed tap already makes {R} per Goblin, so five Goblins pay the {3}{R}{R} untap-and-extra-combat activation from creatures alone — a two-card combat engine with a piece the deck runs, filling the wincon shortfall the role budget flags.
ten.unlocks: Extra combats convert a wide board into wins without the storm count. Note the deck's own trap: Throne of Eldraine's mana is spells-only and cannot pay this activation.

combo_lines_opened.produces: Infinite colorless mana; Infinite creature tokens; Infinite damage; Infinite death triggers; Infinite ETB; Infinite LTB; Infinite red mana; Infinite sacrifice triggers

ten.why: Every Goblin entering adds {C} per Goblin you control, so the verified Empty the Warrens turn (stack 002) pays for its own follow-up — eight tokens entering one at a time generate a rising flood of colorless for buybacks and Grapeshot recasts.
ten.unlocks: Storm mana that scales with the swarm, plus an infinite-flagged line with Prospector and Pashalik Mons, both already sleeved. Generic-heavy costs (buybacks, equip, activations) are the best sinks.

ten.why: The pivot trigger is Zada online with bodies and a cantrip; a spot-removal spell aimed at Zada in response undoes the whole turn, and Swat answers it for zero mana while every other resource is committed to the storm.
ten.unlocks: Free protection on the all-in turn — redirect the kill spell to another target, or retarget an opposing draw spell. Fills the protection shortfall the role budget flags without costing storm mana.

ten.role: draw:burst (tagged buff:pump off its conditional rider)
ten.why: It targets a player, never only Zada, so it is storm fuel and card selection — one storm count plus draw-two at instant speed — not a copy payoff; its mandatory discard is the deck's cheapest way to bin Past in Flames or Wild Ride for later flashback and harmonize.
ten.when: Sleeve it against a creature-light pod (spellslinger, superfriends, stax) where Spreading Insurrection has nothing to steal — and never when an opponent runs graveyard exile, which turns the discard from deferred value into pure loss.

gaps: Every combo line the ten opens is unverified — a line is fact only once a stack artifact passes the checker. Highest-value scenario first: Seething Anger's loop arithmetic (Treasures per cast versus the {3}{R} buyback recast at N creatures — find N).

Aggravated Assault + Howlsquad Heavy assumes max speed is reached and five Goblins can tap; the start-your-engines timing needs a stack scenario before the two-card claim is presented as more than a lead.
The deck runs 36 lands against the provisional 36-land budget, so there is no land gap to argue about; the strategy corpus was not consulted for a storm-deck land floor either way.
sideboard-facts reports no EDHREC rank for Sazacap's Brew, so its popularity signal is absent; the keep case rests entirely on this deck's needs.

Underworld Breach is the full-step option beyond this ten — a Game Changer that rebuilds the storm from the graveyard alongside Past in Flames. It needs a graveyard-count plus Grapeshot stack scenario before it can be ranked honestly.
